key_insight: Human–machine interactions across the entire AI lifecycle—not just at single decision points—determine the real degree of human control in military systems, so governance must shift from isolated rules to lifecycle-aware, sociotechnical oversight.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between assumptions of meaningful human control and the dispersed, cumulative effects of design, training, deployment, and monitoring practices that weaken accountability and decision-making in military AI.
method: Conceptual analysis mapping human–machine interaction points across the AI lifecycle (design, data, training, deployment, monitoring, feedback).
Critical examination of governance gaps and institutional responsibilities that arise from distributed decision-making and automation practices.
Policy-oriented recommendations for sociotechnical controls, transparency, and governance mechanisms to preserve meaningful human oversight.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reframes system design choices as governance decisions: documentation, interface design, monitoring, and human-in-the-loop practices materially affect control and accountability. Adopting lifecycle-aware practices reduces legal, ethical, and operational risks in military AI deployments.
visual_elements: AI lifecycle diagram highlighting human touchpoints (data → training → deployment → monitoring → feedback).
Flowchart showing how design choices propagate to decision-making authority and accountability gaps.
Layered governance infographic (technical, operational, legal) with examples of interventions at each layer.
Icon set for key concepts: human-in-the-loop, accountability, transparency, risk/uncertainty.
paper_title: Re-thinking human–machine interaction and the governance of AI in the military domain
